title: Remark
body_md: Finding a matrix criterion that guarantees the nonsingularity of the matrices $\widehat \mathbf{C}_n$ under the weakly well-conditioning of the family $\{\mathbf{C}_n\}_n$ should be interesting. A necessary condition is clearly the nonsingularity of the two perturbed blocks of size $(m+k) \times (m+k)$ in \eqref{eq:43}, but this is not sufficient (see Example \ref{ex:A7}). A sufficient condition, however difficult to verify in our case, is given in Remark \ref{rem:A6}, the proof of which is deduced from the proof of Theorem \ref{th:45} and \cite[Remark 2]{AmodioBrugnano1996}. At present, to apply Theorem \ref{th:45} to the families $\{\mathbf{K}_n^p(\rho,\delta)\}_n$ in \eqref{eq:310} we have to assume the nonsingularity of their elements as in Assumption \ref{assu:1}.

label: lem:47
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:47}
Let the family of matrices $\{\mathbf{G}_n^p\}_n$ be as in \eqref{eq:44}, and, if $p>1$, assume that not all the zeros of $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$, defined in \eqref{eq:45}, are on the boundary of the unit circle. Then, $\{\mathbf{G}_n^p\}_n$ is weakly well-conditioned if and only if the associated polynomial $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ has exactly two zeros of unit modulus.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Assume $p>1$, if $p=1$ the proof is analogous. According to Theorem \ref{th:41}, the matrix family $\{\mathbf{G}_n^p\}_n$ exhibits weakly well-conditioned, or well-conditioned, behaviour if and only if $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ falls into one of the following types: $(r_1,p+1-r_1,p-1)$ for some $r_1 \in \{0,\ldots,p+1\}$ or $(p+1,p-1-r_2,r_2)$ for some $r_2 \in \{0,\ldots,p-1\}$. It is worth noting that if $\xi$ is a zero of $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$, then $\xi^{-1}$ is also a zero. Hence, $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ necessarily is a polynomial of type $(r,2p-2r,r)$ for some $r \in \{1,\ldots,p\}$. Consequently, the only admissible choice for weakly well-conditioning is $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ of type $(p-1,2,p-1)$.
head: environment

label: lem:48
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:48}
If $p>1$, assume that not all the zeros of $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ in \eqref{eq:45} are on the boundary of the unit circle. Then, the family of matrices $\{ \mathbf{G}_n^p \}_n$ as defined in \eqref{eq:44} exhibits weakly well-conditioned behaviour if and only if the Chebyshev transform $\mathcal{T} q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ \eqref{eq:46} of the polynomial $q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$ has exactly one real root in the interval $[-2,2]$.
head: environment

label: lem:49
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: To prove the first formula, let us consider $f(x) = \mathcal{T} q^{\mathbf{G}^p}(x+2)$. For all roots $x_j$ of $\mathcal{T} q^{\mathbf{G}^p}$, we have $f(x_j-2)=\mathcal{T} q^{\mathbf{G}^p}(x_j)=0$. Therefore, recalling Vieta's formulas the product $(x_1-2)\dots(x_p-2)$ is equal to $(-1)^p f(0)/g_0$. We can compute $f(0) = \mathcal{T} q^{\mathbf{G}^p}(2) = q^{\mathbf{G}^p}(1)$, the latter because $x(z) = z^{-1} + z = 2$ if and only if $z=1$. For the second formula, the proof follows a similar reasoning.

body_md: The statement of Proposition \ref{prop:51} exhibits a close connection to \cite[Lemma 6]{GaroniManniPelosiSerraCapizzanoSpeleers2014} and \cite[Lemma 7]{GaroniManniPelosiSerraCapizzanoSpeleers2014}, where the authors investigate the symbols of matrices associated with IgA discretizations. Specifically, the $p^{\operatorname{th}}$ symbol is $e_p(\theta) = f_p(\theta) / g_p(\theta)$, as detailed in, for example, \cite[Equation 15]{EkstromFurciGaroniManniSerraCapizzano2018}, where $f_p(\theta) = -B_p(\theta)$ and $g_p(\theta) = M_p(\theta)$. For an extensive discussion on how symbols are used to derive analytical spectral properties for IgA discretization of boundary value problems, see \cite{GaroniSpeleersEkstromRealiSerraCapizzanoHughes2019} and the references provided therein.

label: rem:A6
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:A6}
With a similar idea as in the previous remark, we also deduce a criterion to guarantee the nonsingularity of the elements of the family $\{\widehat \mathbf{C}_n\}_n$. Let the family of nonsingular Toeplitz band matrices $\{\mathbf{C}_n\}_n$ be weakly well-conditioned with $q^{\mathbf{C}}$ of type $(m_1,m_2,k)$ with $m_1+m_2=m$, and let $\{\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_n\}_n$ be a family of perturbed matrices with perturbation as in the assumption of Theorem \ref{th:45}. If the matrix $\mathbf{G}_2^{(1)}$ associated with the family $\{\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_n\}_n$ and $\mathbf{G}_2^{(1)}$ associated with $\{\mathbf{J}_n (\widehat{\mathbf{C}}_n)^\top \mathbf{J}_n\}_n$, being $\mathbf{J}_n$ as defined in \eqref{eq:A13}, are nonsingular, then for $n$ sufficiently large, each $\widehat\mathbf{C}_n$ is nonsingular. In our case, it is difficult to verify this criterion for the families $\{\mathbf{K}_n^p(\rho,\delta)\}_n$ since the Casorati matrix $\mathbf{W}$ involves the zero of the associated polynomial $q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho,\delta)}$, which are difficult to obtain due to dependence on the parameters $\rho$ and $\delta$.
